nodes.label: juan-garibay-portfolio (repo overview)
nodes.rationale: A portfolio of seven internal tools published with the evidence behind each one rather than a description of it. Code is published to be read, not reused.

nodes.label: js/data.js — single source of truth for every figure
nodes.rationale: Every figure on the site is authored in exactly one place so that every other copy can be mechanically checked against it instead of maintained by memory.

nodes.label: The four-copy drift problem
nodes.rationale: The same facts live in four places (js/data.js, the noscript block, the JSON-LD block, the static hero) and only one is visible on a normal page load, so three drift silently. Both had already drifted: the fallback was two measurement rounds behind and the structured data had lost a whole project and carried a reworded description.

nodes.label: check.mjs consistency guard (npm run check)
nodes.rationale: Reads js/data.js and fails if any copy disagrees with it. Proves the page is internally consistent; npm run measure is what proves it is true. node check.mjs is the whole tooling story — nothing to install.

nodes.label: Fallback check scoped to the noscript block
nodes.rationale: An earlier version searched the whole document, so a stale figure in the fallback could hide behind a correct one in the hero. That is the kind of bug a guard is supposed to catch, not have.

nodes.label: README deliberately restates no figures
nodes.rationale: Quoting counts or dates in the README would make it a fifth copy of the data that nothing guards.

nodes.label: No dependencies, no build step, no framework
nodes.rationale: Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript served as files; the site runs from python3 -m http.server with nothing to install.

nodes.label: Figures are measured and carry their measurement date
nodes.rationale: One fixed line-count method across all builds — authored source only, excluding dependencies, build output, third-party libraries and generated files. Counting another way moves the numbers by up to three times, so the method has to travel with them. Systems are still in active development, so figures are a snapshot rather than a ceiling.

nodes.label: Contrast is computed, not eyeballed
nodes.rationale: Every token was checked against the background it is actually painted on, not against the page ground — a colour that passes on the body can fail on a card, and one did.

nodes.label: Layout shift fixed at the source, not reserved with min-height
nodes.rationale: The placeholder headline was one line and the real one is five, so reserving space could not work. Writing the real hero into the HTML took measured CLS on a throttled load from 0.110 to 0 on desktop and tablet; what remains on narrow viewports is webfont swap, not layout (0 with fonts blocked).

nodes.label: A failed render says so
nodes.rationale: If the script throws, a banner is shown rather than letting a reader take the stored fallback for current figures, and the thrown error names the stage that failed.

nodes.label: Built to be printed
nodes.rationale: Someone will print this for a meeting, so the print stylesheet inverts to ink on paper, drops screenshots, and resolves every link to its destination since paper cannot be clicked.

nodes.label: tools/encode-demo.sh — demo recording encoder
nodes.rationale: Turns a raw screen recording into the three files a project card needs — H.264, VP9 and a poster frame — and prints a demo block to paste into js/data.js. Cards render video with preload=none so it costs nothing until someone presses play; audio is stripped and clips stay 20-35 seconds.

nodes.label: Record demos against seeded data only
nodes.rationale: These pages are public and a recording of an internal tool shows whatever data is loaded — customer names, addresses, prices, margins. Currents is the only demo on the site precisely because it holds no business data; the route planner shows the customer master and the Farmers Fresh quoting tool still has access control disabled.

nodes.label: Business case rests on low-confidence assumptions
nodes.rationale: The source document rates the business-case assumptions low confidence with measurement dates still ahead of them, so they are marked as estimates on the page and in the data. The engineering figures — line counts, commits, tests, contrast, layout shift — are measured, reproducible and dated.

nodes.label: No licence granted
nodes.rationale: The code is published to be read, not reused.
